Question
========
The `diamonds` dataset is built into ggplot2 and contains information on about 54,000 diamonds, including their `carat`, `price` and `cut`.

Write R code that creates a scatterplot of `price` (y-axis) against `carat` (x-axis) using the `diamonds` dataset, where the points are coloured according to `cut`.


Solution
========
```
ggplot(data = diamonds, mapping = aes(x = carat, y = price, colour = cut)) +
  geom_point()
```

The call to `ggplot()` sets up the plot object, passing `diamonds` as the data and mapping `carat` to the x-axis, `price` to the y-axis, and `cut` to the colour aesthetic. Adding `geom_point()` as a layer is what actually renders the points - without at least one layer, nothing would be drawn.
